   528	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_directSum {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   529	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   530	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   531	    (ell : ℕ) (t : J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell)
   532	    (ht : ∀ j, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (t j) (V j)) (x : ι → K) :
   533	    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t) x =
   534	      ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   535	  induction ell generalizing V x with
   536	  | zero =>
   537	      apply Eq.symm
   538	      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   539	      intro j _
   540	      cases t j
   541	      rfl
   542	  | succ ell ih =>
   543	      let S : J → Finset ι := fun j => (t j).headSupport
   544	      let y : J → ι → K := fun j =>
   545	        (t j).headLinear (coordinateRestriction (S j) x)
   546	      have hS (j : J) : S j ⊆ V j :=
   547	        CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_headSupport (ht j)
   548	      have hy (j : J) (a : ι) (ha : a ∉ V j) : y j a = 0 := by
   549	        exact CondLinearTerm.headLinear_eq_zero_of_not_mem (t j) _
   550	          (fun haS => ha (hS j haS))
   551	      have hhead :
   552	          condLinearHeadSum t
   553	              (coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ.biUnion S) x) = ∑ j, y j := by
   554	        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   555	        intro j _
   556	        change (t j).headLinear
   557	            (coordinateRestriction (S j)
   558	              (coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ.biUnion S) x)) =
   559	          (t j).headLinear (coordinateRestriction (S j) x)
   560	        rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction
   561	          (Finset.subset_biUnion_of_mem S (Finset.mem_univ j))]
   562	      have hselect (j : J) : coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, y i) = y j :=
   563	        coordinateRestriction_sum_eq V hDisjoint y hy j
   564	      have htail (j : J) :
   565	          CondLinearTerm.supportedOn ((t j).tail (y j)) (V j \ S j) := by
   566	        exact CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_tail (ht j) (y j)
   567	      have hDisjointTail : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
   568	          Disjoint (V i \ S i) (V j \ S j) := by
   569	        intro i j hij
   570	        exact (hDisjoint i j hij).mono Finset.sdiff_subset Finset.sdiff_subset
   571	      have htail_eval (j : J) :
   572	          CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   573	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) =
   574	            CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   575	              (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   576	        have hrestrict := CondLinearTerm.eval_coordinateRestriction
   577	          (htail j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
   578	        rwa [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction Finset.sdiff_subset] at hrestrict
   579	      have hcomponent (j : J) :
   580	          CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) =
   581	            y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   582	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) := by
   583	        rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_succ_eq]
   584	        change (t j).headLinear
   585	              (coordinateRestriction (S j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) +
   586	            CondLinearTerm.eval
   587	              ((t j).tail
   588	                ((t j).headLinear
   589	                  (coordinateRestriction (S j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x))))
   590	              (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) = _
   591	        rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction (hS j)]
   592	        change y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   593	            (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) = _
   594	        rw [htail_eval]
   595	      have hrec := ih (fun j => V j \ S j) hDisjointTail
   596	        (fun j => (t j).tail (y j)) htail x
   597	      have htail_family :
   598	          (fun j => (t j).tail (coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, y i))) =
   599	            (fun j => (t j).tail (y j)) := by
   600	        funext j
   601	        rw [hselect]
   602	      calc
   603	        CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.directSum V (ell + 1) t) x =
   604	            (∑ j, y j) +
   605	              CondLinearTerm.eval
   606	                (CondLinearTerm.directSum (fun j => V j \ S j) ell
   607	                  (fun j => (t j).tail (y j))) x := by
   608	              change condLinearHeadSum t
   609	                    (coordinateRestriction
   610	                      (Finset.univ.biUnion fun j => (t j).headSupport) x) +
   611	                  CondLinearTerm.eval
   612	                    (CondLinearTerm.directSum
   613	                      (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) ell
   614	                      (fun j => (t j).tail
   615	                        (coordinateRestriction (V j)
   616	                          (condLinearHeadSum t
   617	                            (coordinateRestriction
   618	                              (Finset.univ.biUnion fun i => (t i).headSupport) x))))) x = _
   619	              rw [show (fun j => (t j).headSupport) = S from rfl, hhead]
   620	              rw [htail_family]
   621	        _ = (∑ j, y j) + ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   622	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) := by rw [hrec]
   623	        _ = ∑ j, (y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   624	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x)) := Finset.sum_add_distrib.symm
   625	        _ = ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   626	              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   627	              intro j _
   628	              exact (hcomponent j).symm
   629	
   630	/-- Equal-level direct sums of maps on disjoint registers are conditionally
   631	linear on the union of those registers.  This is a formalization-only
   632	auxiliary for `lem:cl-func-prod`, blueprint
   633	`lem:cl-func-prod-same-level`. -/
   634	theorem IsCondLinearOn.directSum_sameLevel {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   635	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   636	    (V : J → Finset ι) (ell : ℕ) (L : J → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   637	    (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   638	    (hL : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) ell (L j)) :
   639	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ.biUnion V) ell
   640	      (fun x => ∑ j, L j (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) := by
   641	  classical
   642	  choose t ht ht_eval using hL
   643	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t,
   644	    CondLinearTerm.directSum_supportedOn V hDisjoint ell t ht, ?_⟩
   645	  funext x
   646	  rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_directSum V hDisjoint ell t ht x]
   647	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   648	  intro j _
   649	  exact congrFun (ht_eval j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
   650	
   651	/--
   652	The distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common
   653	uniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in
   654	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1067-1070`, paper origin
   655	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.
   656	-/
   657	noncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   658	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   659	    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
   660	  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))
   661	
   662	/-- The direct-sum map used to encode the paper's CL concatenation.  The left
   663	coordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member
   664	`R u v` selected by the left input `u`.  This is Lean-only coordinate
   665	infrastructure for `lem:cl-concat`, blueprint
   666	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1103-1117`, paper origin
   667	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   668	-/
   669	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   670	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   671	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   672	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   673	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
   674	  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)
   675	  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)
   676	
   677	/--
   678	Concatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is
   679	`lem:cl-concat` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1103-1117`, with
   680	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:282-314`.
   681	The map `condLinearConcat` realizes this concatenation on the direct sum.
   682	-/
   683	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   684	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   685	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   686	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}
   687	    (hL : IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιU) k L)
   688	    (hR : ∀ u : ιU → K, u ∈ Set.range L →
   689	      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :
   690	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)
   691	      (condLinearConcat L R) := by
   692	  classical
   693	  rcases hL with ⟨tL, htL, htL_eval⟩
   694	  let rTerm : (ιU → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell := fun u =>
   695	    if hu : u ∈ Set.range L then Classical.choose (hR u hu)
   696	    else CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel ell
   697	  have hr_supported (u : ιU → K) :
   698	      CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rTerm u) (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) := by
   699	    by_cases hu : u ∈ Set.range L
   700	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   701	      exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).1
   702	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_neg hu]
   703	      exact CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel_supportedOn ell Finset.univ
   704	  have hr_eval (u : ιU → K) (hu : u ∈ Set.range L) :
   705	      CondLinearTerm.eval (rTerm u) = R u := by
   706	    simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   707	    exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).2
   708	  rw [Nat.add_comm k ell]
   709	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.concat rTerm 0 tL, ?_, ?_⟩
   710	  · have hsupport := CondLinearTerm.concat_supportedOn
   711	      (acc := (0 : ιU → K)) htL hr_supported
   712	    have huniv :
   713	        (Finset.univ : Finset ιU).map Function.Embedding.inl ∪
   714	            (Finset.univ : Finset ιV).map Function.Embedding.inr =
   715	          (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) := by
   716	      ext i
   717	      cases i <;> simp
   718	    simpa only [huniv] using hsupport
   719	  · funext x
   720	    rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_concat]
   721	    simp only [zero_add]
   722	    rw [congrFun htL_eval (fun i => x (.inl i))]
   723	    rw [hr_eval (L (fun i => x (.inl i))) ⟨_, rfl⟩]
   724	    rfl
   725	
   726	/--
   727	The graph distribution is uniform on ordered pairs `(a, b)` whose unordered
   728	pair belongs to `E`, including self-loops.  This is `def:graph-distribution`
   729	in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1233-1245`;
   730	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:984-1009`.
   731	The underlying graph-distribution definition is
   732	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.
   733	-/
   734	noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   735	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
   736	  Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   737	    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)
   738	
   739	/-- The graph distribution has total mass one whenever its edge set is
   740	nonempty.  This is not a named statement of the source article; it is
   741	`lem:graph-distribution-mass` in
   742	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1247-1257`. -/
   743	theorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   744	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :
   745	    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by
   746	  apply Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability
   747	  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := hE
   748	  obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, rfl⟩ := Sym2.mk_surjective e
   749	  change s(a, b) ∈ E at he
   750	  exact ⟨(a, b), Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, he⟩⟩
   751

    72	/-- Conditional linearity is monotone in the number of levels. -/

   157	private theorem sum_coordinateRestriction_eq {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   158	    [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]

   162	  classical
   163	  ext a
   164	  obtain ⟨j, haj⟩ := hCover a
   165	  rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_eq_single j]
   166	  · simp [coordinateRestriction, haj]
   167	  · intro i _ hij
   168	    have hai : a ∉ V i := fun hai =>
   169	      Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai haj
   170	    simp [coordinateRestriction, hai]
   171	  · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim

   179	  classical
   180	  constructor
   181	  · intro h j
   182	    rw [← h]
   183	    exact (coordinateRestriction_sum_eq V hDisjoint f hf j).symm
   184	  · intro h

   186	      (∑ j, f j) = ∑ j, coordinateRestriction (V j) x := by
   187	        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => h j
   188	      _ = x := sum_coordinateRestriction_eq V hDisjoint hCover x

   296	        linear := fun _ _ => L₁.comp (coordinateRestrictionLinear S₁)

   298	        factor_subset := ?_
   299	        factor_disjoint := ?_

   301	        linear_supported := ?_
   302	        sum_formula := ?_
   303	        top := ?_

   305	      · intro k
   306	        have hk : k = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
   307	        subst k
   308	        exact ⟨.succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest, ht, rfl⟩
   309	      · intro k u
   310	        exact Finset.Subset.rfl
   311	      · intro x i j hij
   312	        exact (hij (Subsingleton.elim i j)).elim
   313	      · intro x a ha

275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.
   281	
   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}

   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}
   374	
   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.
   378	  By Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}, this is equivalent to the distribution over
   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.
   381	  This distribution is exactly the product of the distributions $
   382	  \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$.
   383	\end{proof}

    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.

    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,
    73	  \begin{equation*}
    74	    \mu_G(u, v) =
    75	    \begin{cases}

    80	  This is identical to the uniform distribution over pairs $(u, v)\in U\times U$
    81	  such that $\{u, v\} \in E$.

1	# Formalization Patterns
     2	
     3	Key design patterns used in the MIPStarRE Lean formalization to bridge the
     4	gap between paper-level mathematics and a compilable Lean proof.
     5	
     6	This document is intended for contributors who need to understand *why* the
     7	Lean code is structured as it is, and for reviewers who need to recognize
     8	these patterns when reading PRs.  It complements the individual chapter audits
     9	in `audits/`, the proof-integrity rules in the lean-conventions skill (addenda:
    10	`docs/project_conventions.md`), and the
    11	proof-gap protocol in `docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.
    12	
    13	## Table of Contents
    14	
    15	1. [Source-faithful statements and internal proof obligations](#pattern-1-source-faithful-statements-and-internal-proof-obligations)
    16	2. [Blueprint–Lean synchronization](#pattern-2-blueprintlean-synchronization)
    17	3. [Split-module architecture](#pattern-3-split-module-architecture)
    18	4. [Public re-export pattern](#pattern-4-public-re-export-pattern)
    19	5. [Temporary obligation-structure pattern](#pattern-5-temporary-obligation-structure-pattern)
    20	6. [Paper-gap documentation pattern](#pattern-6-paper-gap-documentation-pattern)
    21	
    22	---
    23	
    24	## Pattern 1: Source-faithful statements and internal proof obligations
    25	
    26	### The rule
    27	
    28	A declaration presented as the formalization of a paper theorem, lemma,
    29	proposition, or corollary must state the paper result, up to faithful formal
    30	encoding of the mathematical domain.  Its public hypotheses and conclusion are
    31	both part of the statement.  Adding a load-bearing bridge, residual, repair,
    32	obligation-structure input, hypotheses bundle, or assumptions bundle not present
    33	in the cited statement changes the theorem into a conditional helper.
    34	
    35	The project therefore distinguishes three objects.
    36	
    37	| Object | Public statement | Blueprint status |
    38	|--------|------------------|------------------|
    39	| Paper theorem | Matches the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/` | May be linked by source-labelled `\lean{}`; statement-level `\leanok` only when the statement matches |
    40	| Internal proof obligation | Proves a missing intermediate mathematical input from paper hypotheses | May contain a tracked `sorry` while the proof is open |
    41	| Conditional helper | Quarantines an unproved intermediate obligation | Not a paper theorem; no source-labelled `\leanok` |
    42	
    43	It is never allowed to change the public statement of a declaration presented
    44	as the formalization of a source-labelled paper theorem.  At the final assembly
    45	point, the paper theorem must either discharge the extra hypotheses internally,
    46	or remain as the paper-aligned statement with an unfinished proof while the
    47	conditional helper is given a different name.
    48	
    49	The preferred way to expose unfinished work is a named internal theorem or
    50	definition with a precise paper-origin docstring and, if necessary, a tracked
    51	`sorry`.  This makes the proof frontier visible without weakening the statement
    52	of a source-labelled theorem.
    53	
    54	### Why legacy scaffolding may remain temporarily
    55	
    56	| Temporary reason | Explanation |
    57	|------------------|-------------|
    58	| **Localizing an obstruction** | A conditional helper can isolate the exact missing mathematical input while the obligation discharger is being proved. |
    59	| **Recovering useful proof content** | The proof body may contain genuine estimates or constructions that should be extracted into source-faithful lemmas. |
    60	| **Auditability** | An explicit temporary hypothesis is easier to find than an implicit assumption hidden in prose, provided it is named as proof debt. |
    61	
    62	These reasons do not justify strengthening a paper theorem.  They only explain
    63	why a short-lived helper declaration may exist while its remaining hypotheses
    64	are being actively removed.
    65	
    66	### How to proceed when a proof needs an extra input
    67	
    68	1. **Check the source statement.**  Read the corresponding TeX in
    69	   `references/ldt-paper/` before changing a theorem linked from the blueprint.
    70	2. **Keep the paper-facing declaration source-faithful.**  Boundary hypotheses
    71	   such as positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances, or
    72	   type-class assumptions may be faithful encodings when they are needed to
    73	   state the mathematics in Lean.  Proof data such as `BridgeInputs`,
    74	   `RepairInput`, `Residual`, `Package`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic
    75	   `Assumptions` is different: it is not a paper assumption unless the cited
    76	   statement says so.
    77	3. **Name the missing intermediate result.**  If the proof uses a mathematical
    78	   fact not yet formalized, state it as a separate proof obligation.  A
    79	   temporary `sorry` in this declaration is preferable to adding the obligation as
    80	   a hypothesis on the paper theorem.
    81	4. **Do not introduce conditional helpers by default.**  A helper whose name
    82	   ends in `_ofObligations` is a quarantine device, not a normal formalization
    83	   pattern.  It may remain temporarily only when it preserves substantial proof
    84	   content that cannot yet be connected to the paper hypotheses, has a tracked
    85	   discharge or deletion target, and has no source-labelled blueprint
    86	   `\leanok`.  If the helper would merely package missing work as an extra
    87	   hypothesis, restore the theorem with the paper statement and leave a tracked
    88	   `sorry` instead.
    89	5. **Audit the final statement.**  Every PR touching a source-labelled theorem
    90	   should compare paper assumptions and Lean assumptions, paper conclusion and
    91	   Lean conclusion, and report whether the Lean statement is exact, has only
    92	   faithful boundary hypotheses, or has extra assumptions.
    93	
    94	If a paper-facing declaration is temporarily proved by calling a conditional
    95	helper whose load-bearing input has not yet been produced from the paper
    96	hypotheses, the proof frontier must be marked explicitly.  The declaration
    97	should carry an `**Unfaithful:**` docstring section naming the non-paper
    98	dependency, citing the paper-gap note or tracking issue, and identifying the
    99	internal theorem that will remove the dependency.  A named proof obligation
   100	with a tracked `sorry` is preferred whenever possible, because it makes the
   101	missing mathematical assertion visible without adding it to the paper theorem
   102	statement.
   103	
   104	### Required metadata for new proof-obligation declarations
   105	
   106	A new declaration whose name contains a proof-debt token such as `Bridge`,
   107	`Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Producer`, `Input`, `Hypotheses`,
   108	`Assumptions`, `Obligation`, or `Witness` must explain its mathematical role in
   109	the def-site docstring.  A paper citation alone is not enough, because the
   110	reviewer must be able to tell whether the declaration is part of the paper
   111	statement or a Lean-only proof obligation.
   112	
   113	Use one of the following markers.
   114	
   115	| Marker | Use |
   116	|--------|-----|
   117	| `**Source:**`, `**Paper source:**`, or `**Source statement:**` | The declaration is a faithful formal encoding of a cited source statement or a field of that statement |
   118	| `**Faithful encoding:**` | The declaration records boundary data or domain data that the paper uses implicitly |
   119	| `**Proof obligation:**` or `**Internal proof obligation:**` | The declaration is a theorem or record that must be proved from the paper hypotheses before a source theorem is complete |
   120	| `**Conditional:**` | The declaration is a conditional helper; it must not be linked as the source theorem |
   121	| `**Unfaithful:**` | The declaration or proof currently depends on a load-bearing assumption not yet derived from the paper hypotheses |
   122	
   123	Proof-obligation, conditional, and unfaithful markers must cite a paper-gap note
   124	or tracking issue and must state the planned discharge or elimination theorem.
   125	If such a declaration would merely package missing work as an added hypothesis
   126	to a source theorem, do not introduce it; restore the source theorem statement
   127	and leave the missing proof as a tracked `sorry`.
   128	
   129	### Conditional helper boundary
   130	
   131	1. **Prefer a source theorem with a tracked `sorry`.**  If a proof requires a
   132	   construction that is not yet available from the paper hypotheses, the first
   133	   repair is to restore the source theorem statement and leave the missing proof
   134	   open.  Do not introduce a new `Input`, `Obligation`, `Residual`, `Repair`,
   135	   `Producer`, or `Package` merely to avoid that `sorry`.
   136	
   137	2. **Do not bundle several missing theorem-level steps into one hypothesis.**
   138	   The former Section 9 bundle `SelfImprovementObligations` and the helper
   139	   `selfImprovementFromObligations` were removed because they bundled
   140	   helper strong self-consistency, orthonormalization, and final-field transport
   141	   into a single route to the full self-improvement conclusion.  The correct
   142	   boundary is now the theorem `selfImprovement`, whose missing
   143	   proof is an explicit `sorry`.
   144	
   145	   The former induction-section helper
   146	   `selfImprovementInInductionSection_ofObligations` was removed because it
   147	   encouraged propagation of the Section 9 bundle into the Section 6 successor
   148	   constructors.  Those constructors now call the theorem
   149	   `selfImprovementInInductionSection` directly; its current proof gap is the
   150	   correct place for the missing work.
   151	
   152	3. **Propagation is a warning sign.**  The consumer of
   153	   `selfImprovementInInductionSection` — typically a
   154	   `MainInductionStep` theorem — should close the hypothesis with an internal
   155	   theorem as soon as possible.  If the hypothesis propagates upward toward a
   156	   paper-labelled theorem, the PR should stop and either prove the obligation or
   157	   restore the paper theorem with an explicit unfinished proof.
   158	
   159	4. **Final closure at the paper theorem.**  The theorem `mainFormal` in
   160	   `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/MainTheorem/MainFormal.lean` is reserved for the
   161	   paper-shaped statement.  If the witness needed by the final transport has
   162	   not yet been constructed from the paper hypotheses, the theorem should remain
   163	   an explicit unfinished proof.  Do not replace the missing construction by
   164	   extra bridge, residual, repair, package, or obligation hypotheses, and do not
   165	   proliferate named obligation declarations merely to avoid a direct `sorry`.
   166	
   167	   The paper-labelled `mainFormal` should have the hypotheses of the paper
   168	   theorem: a projective strategy passing the low individual degree test, the
   169	   stated parameter bounds, and the faithful formalization of the ambient
   170	   domains.  Bridge, residual, repair, and proof-obligation inputs must be
   171	   produced inside its proof rather than added to its statement.
   172	
   173	### Existing bridge-like declarations
   174	
   175	Several older declarations still name proof obligations explicitly.  They are
   176	transitional proof debt, not a pattern to extend to paper theorem statements.
   177	When such a declaration remains useful, its role should be made explicit and
   178	kept away from source-labelled blueprint entries.
   179	
   180	| Declaration | Status to maintain |
   181	|-------------|--------------------|
   182	| `LdPastingNontrivialContext` | Nontrivial-regime context for `ldPastingNontrivial`; do not present it as the unrestricted `thm:ld-pasting` context |
   183	| `Pasting.ldPastingNontrivial` | Restricted nontrivial-regime form of `thm:ld-pasting`; link from a Lean-only remark, while `Pasting.ldPasting` remains the unrestricted source-facing theorem |
   184	
   185	The former same-carrier `mainFormal` transport-witness route has been retired.
   186	The former `SelfImprovement.HelperStrongSelfConsistencyInput`,
   187	`SelfImprovement.OrthonormalizationInput`, `SelfImprovement.FinalFieldsInput`, and
   188	`MakingMeasurementsProjective.OrthonormalizationInput` bundles have been removed.
   189	Useful proof content should be kept as named construction lemmas, while missing
   190	orthonormalization or final-field arguments remain direct proof gaps on the
   191	source-facing theorem until proved from the paper hypotheses.
   192	
   193	The former `MakingMeasurementsProjective.SpectralTruncationInput` abbreviation
   194	has likewise been retired.  The spectral-truncation step is represented by the
   195	source-shaped statement `SpectralTruncationStatement` and by direct construction
   196	theorems such as `spectralTruncationStatement_of_sourceAlmostProjective`,
   197	rather than by an `Input` wrapper passed through later theorems.
   198	
   199	### Retiring auxiliary declarations
   200	
   201	An auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or
   202	renamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all of the following
   203	conditions hold.
   204	
   205	1. It is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited
   206	   outside result.
   207	2. No current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated.
   208	3. It assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data, repair
   209	   data, synchronization data, or package fields than the paper proof requires.
   210	
   211	If such a declaration is still useful as a formal intermediate result, keep it
   212	as a lemma or a visibly conditional helper with a planned discharge.  It should
   213	not remain a headline replacement for the paper theorem, and it should not be
   214	the target of a source-labelled blueprint `\leanok`.
   215	
   216	### Former proof obligations in `MainFormal.lean`
   217	
   218	The former direct tracked proof obligations in `MainFormal.lean` and the
   219	Section 6 successor route have been discharged under the corrected source
   220	statements.  The theorem `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` is the corrected
   221	two-space source theorem.  The earlier same-carrier auxiliary interface has
   222	been retired; the headline theorem carries no bridge, residual, repair,
   223	package, producer, generic hypothesis, or proof-obligation input in its public
   224	statement.
   225	
   226	### Distinction from anti-patterns
   227	
   228	This rule addresses the same risk as conclusion-shaped-hypothesis smuggling
   229	(anti-pattern A1 in `docs/anti_patterns.md`), but it is stricter for
   230	paper-labelled declarations:
   231	
   232	- A conclusion-shaped hypothesis is always unacceptable.
   233	- A genuine intermediate fact may appear only in a separately named conditional
   234	  helper while its obligation discharger is being proved.
   235	- That same intermediate fact is still unacceptable as an added hypothesis on
   236	  the public statement of the paper theorem, unless it is a faithful encoding
   237	  of a hypothesis present in the cited source.
   238	
   239	Obligation structures that bundle still-unproved theorem-level steps are proof
   240	debt under this pattern.  They should not be introduced merely because a proof

   125	
   126	### Additional rules:
   127	- **Section names in Lean**: use mathematical terms (`section QuantumSoundness`, `section SelfImprovement`, `section PastingLemma`), not organizational terms (`section Assembly`, `section Pipeline`).

   129	- **Definitions that are actually theorems**: if a statement asserts a mathematical fact, it must be `\begin{theorem}`, not `\begin{definition}`. Definitions introduce new objects; theorems prove properties.
   130	
   131	## `\uses` Dependency Guidelines
   132	- **Statement `\uses`**: list only what's needed to *state* the result (typically definitions of the objects involved). Keep minimal — transitive deps are automatic.
   133	- **Proof `\uses`**: list only what the proof *actually calls*. Don't list definitions unless the proof unfolds that definition.
   134	- **Never self-reference**: a proof's `\uses` must NOT include the label of the theorem it proves.
   135	
   136	## Recording Formalization-Only Lemmas
   137	Some Lean lemmas are genuine proof infrastructure rather than named statements
   138	from the original papers. These must be traceable without making the blueprint
   139	look as if the paper stated them.
   140	
   141	- If a declaration directly formalizes a paper or blueprint statement, record
   142	  it as usual with `\lean{...}` on that statement and cite the relevant source.
   143	- If a public declaration is an auxiliary lemma introduced only for the Lean
   144	  proof, make that status explicit. Its Lean docstring should say that it is a
   145	  formalization-only auxiliary lemma and should name the nearby paper equation,
   146	  line range, or blueprint result it supports.

   161	## Blueprint Structure

Only proof-level `\leanok` whose axiom closure contains `sorryAx` (or whose harness output cannot be parsed) is reported as an **error**. Statement-level-only `\leanok` with the same finding is downgraded to a **warning**, because statement-level does not claim proof completeness. Each audit line is annotated with the observed placement so reviewers can tell statement-sync work apart from proof-completion work.

   200	`leanblueprint` does not use distinct macro names for these two claims, so audits must distinguish them by environment context rather than by raw `\leanok` counts. A future split such as `\leanokstmt` / `\leanokproof` could make that distinction explicit, but that is only a possible later cleanup; the current convention is to keep `\leanok` and rely on placement.

   202	A recurring historical example is the chapter 4 `Q/X/\widehat X/P` witness
   203	layer.  Once Lean has construction theorems deriving the displayed identities
   204	and estimates from the rank-reduction, sigma-range, positive-Gram, native
   205	spectral-theorem, or rectangular-SVD hypotheses, the corresponding blueprint
   206	entries may carry `\leanok`.  A declaration that merely projects an identity
   207	from an opaque data record is not enough by itself, and a theorem depending on
   208	extra rectangular-SVD data should not be used as evidence for an unconditional
   209	paper statement unless a separate construction supplies that data.
   210	
   211	## Dependency Graph Colors (web)
   212	- **Light green box**: definition with `\lean` + `\leanok` (defined in Lean)
   213	- **Green**: theorem/lemma/proposition/corollary with `\lean` + statement-level `\leanok` (statement matched in Lean)
   214	- **Dark green**: either (i) theorem/lemma/proposition/corollary with both statement-level and proof-level `\leanok` (fully formalized in Lean), or (ii) a `\mathlibok` node
   215	- **Blue**: ready to state/prove (all deps are done)
   216	- **Orange**: `\notready` (needs more blueprint work)
   217	
   218	## Bibliography Workflow
   219	1. Edit `blueprint/src/references.bib` (standalone, AuthorYYYYKeyword keys)
   220	2. Run `texra-blueprint bbl` from the repository root — it regenerates
   221	   `blueprint/src/web.bbl` from the `\cite` keys in the blueprint sources.
   222	   `web.bbl` is not committed (`.gitignore` covers `*.bbl`); every CI job
   223	   that runs the web build regenerates it first, and so must a local run.
   224	3. Run `leanblueprint web` (plasTeX reads `web.bbl`)
   225	4. The PDF build needs no separate step: `leanblueprint pdf` runs bibtex on
   226	   `print.tex` itself, and `print.bbl` never feeds the web build.
   227	5. Citation key format: e.g., `Ji2020MIPStar`, `Natarajan2020Quantum`
   228	6. Paper-gap notes: blueprint prose cites `\cite{gap:<slug>}` (never the raw
   229	   `docs/paper-gaps/<slug>.tex` path); each cited note has a `@techreport`
   230	   entry in `blueprint/src/references.bib` with `type = {Paper-gap note}`,
   231	   whose `note` field carries the published PDF URL as `\url{...}` (the
   232	   alpha style of the PDF build drops `url` fields for techreport entries).
   233	   `texra-blueprint bbl` renders such entries with slug-shaped citation
   234	   labels (e.g. `[issue-906-main-formal-k-bound]`) in the web bibliography,
   235	   while ordinary entries keep alpha labels. Lean docstrings and comments
   236	   keep the repository path form.
   237	
   238	## Stale/Corrupt Aux File Recovery
   239	If LaTeX reports `! File ended while scanning use of \@newl@bel` on startup:
   240	- The `.aux` file was truncated by a previous killed/timed-out run
   241	- Fix: `rm -f blueprint/src/print.aux blueprint/print/print.aux blueprint/print.aux`
   242	- Then rerun latexmk — it rebuilds the aux from scratch cleanly
   243	- `web.bbl` is unaffected: it comes from `texra-blueprint bbl`, not from
   244	  `print.bbl`

   249	leanblueprint web     # HTML → blueprint/web/
   250	leanblueprint serve   # local server at http://0.0.0.0:8000/
   251	leanblueprint all     # pdf + web + checkdecls

   100	## What NOT to Put in the Blueprint
   101	- **Lean identifier names in math text.** Write "the self-improvement lemma", never "the `selfImprovement` step". The `\lean{LDT.selfImprovement}` tag handles the linking.
   102	- **Implementation details.** Don't say "bundled as an element of the Euclidean space" or "using `EuclideanSpace.equiv`". Describe the mathematical object.
   103	- **Ad-hoc notation.** Don't invent superscripts or subscripts to distinguish from existing notation. Use standard conventions.
   104	- **Function-call syntax.** Use mathematical notation, not programming notation.
   105	- **Redundant definitions.** If two blueprint definitions describe the same mathematical object, consolidate them. Each definition should introduce genuinely new mathematical content.
   106	- **Lean namespace prefixes in prose.** Don't write "the `LDT.PastingLemma`" — write "the pasting lemma".
   107	
   108	## Banned AI/Software Language (enforced in both blueprint AND Lean code)
   109	The blueprint reads as a **mathematical document**, not software documentation. The following patterns are banned in ALL reader-facing text (section titles, theorem names, proof sketches, remarks, chapter preambles) and in ALL Lean docstrings, comments, and section names:
   110	
   111	### Banned terms → replacements:
   112	| Banned | Use instead |
   113	|--------|------------|
   114	| "Assembly" (as section/chapter title) | "Proof of [theorem]", "Construction", "Composition" |
   115	| "Pipeline" | "reduction", "construction", "proof chain" |
   116	| "Bridge" (as noun for a connection) | "connection", name by mathematical content |
   117	| "Handoff" / "hand off" | "transition", "continuation", or drop entirely |
   118	| "In this blueprint" / "Within this blueprint" | "here", "in what follows", or omit |
   119	| "Honest" (as adjective for rigorous) | "exact", "faithful", "unconditional", "complete" |
   120	| "Glue layer" | "intermediate construction", "connecting results" |
   121	| "Re-export" / "reexport" | "provides", "re-states" |
   122	| "Wiring" / "wire up" | "connecting", "composing", "combining" |
   123	| "Package" (as noun for a data bundle) | "form", "data", "structure" |
   124	| "Sorry-free" | acceptable only in Lean-specific technical context |
   125	
   126	### Additional rules:
   127	- **Section names in Lean**: use mathematical terms (`section QuantumSoundness`, `section SelfImprovement`, `section PastingLemma`), not organizational terms (`section Assembly`, `section Pipeline`).
   128	- **Internal LaTeX labels** (e.g., `\label{ch:soundness}`) are not reader-facing and need not be renamed if doing so would break cross-references. But NEW labels should follow the standard.
   129	- **Definitions that are actually theorems**: if a statement asserts a mathematical fact, it must be `\begin{theorem}`, not `\begin{definition}`. Definitions introduce new objects; theorems prove properties.
   130	
   131	## `\uses` Dependency Guidelines
   132	- **Statement `\uses`**: list only what's needed to *state* the result (typically definitions of the objects involved). Keep minimal — transitive deps are automatic.
   133	- **Proof `\uses`**: list only what the proof *actually calls*. Don't list definitions unless the proof unfolds that definition.
   134	- **Never self-reference**: a proof's `\uses` must NOT include the label of the theorem it proves.
   135

+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}

+private noncomputable def coordinatePartitionEquiv {K ι J : Type*}
+    [AddCommMonoid K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
+    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) : (ι → K) ≃ ∀ j, V j → K where
+  toFun x := fun _ a => x a
+  invFun x := ∑ j, extendRegister (V j) (x j)
+  left_inv x := by
+    funext a
+    obtain ⟨j, haj⟩ := hCover a
+    change (∑ i, extendRegister (V i) (fun b => x b)) a = x a
+    rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_eq_single j]
+    · simp [extendRegister, haj]
+    · intro i _ hij
+      have hai : a ∉ V i := fun hai =>
+        Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai haj
+      simp [extendRegister, hai]
+    · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim
+  right_inv x := by
+    funext j a
+    change (∑ i, extendRegister (V i) (x i)) a.1 = x j a
+    rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_eq_single j]
+    · simp [extendRegister, a.2]
+    · intro i _ hij
+      have hai : a.1 ∉ V i := fun hai =>
+        Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai a.2
+      simp [extendRegister, hai]
+    · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim

+    [AddCommMonoid K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
+    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) (x : ι → K) (j : J) (a : V j) :
+    coordinatePartitionEquiv V hDisjoint hCover x j a = x a := rfl
+private theorem extendRegister_partition_apply {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
+    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) (x : ι → K) (j : J) :
+    extendRegister (V j) (coordinatePartitionEquiv V hDisjoint hCover x j) =
+      coordinateRestriction (V j) x := by
+  ext a
+  by_cases ha : a ∈ V j
+  · simp [extendRegister, coordinateRestriction, ha, coordinatePartitionEquiv_apply]

+    (Finset.univ.filter p).card = (Finset.univ.filter q).card := by
+  classical

+    ext b
+    simp only [Finset.mem_map, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
+    constructor
+    · rintro ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩

+      exact ⟨e.symm b, (hpq (e.symm b)).mpr (by simpa using hb), by simp⟩

     3	/-!
     4	# Conditionally linear functions and graph distributions
     5	
     6	The question distributions in the Pauli basis test are generated by a finite
     7	graph of types and a shared seed, with each type applying a conditionally linear
     8	map to that seed.  The inductive predicate below records the level structure
     9	needed by later formalization stages.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The source-facing nodes are `def:cl-func`
    14	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`), `def:cl-dist`
    15	(`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1067-1070`), `lem:cl-concat`
    16	(`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1103-1117`), and `def:graph-distribution`
    17	(`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1233-1245`).
    18	The paper origins are
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57,282-314`,
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`,
    21	and `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1010`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    27	
    28	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    29	
    30	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    31	
    32	/--
    33	The source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive
    34	predicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is
    35	rejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same
    36	public predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together
    37	with its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation
    38	deviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes
    39	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`,
    40	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    41	-/
    42	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    43	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    44	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    45	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    46	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    47	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    48	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    49	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
    50	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)
    51	
    52	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary
    53	coordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,
    54	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    55	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    56	-/
    57	def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    58	  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0
    59	
    60	/-- Evaluation of a representation of a conditionally linear function.
    61	Lean-only support for `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    62	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    63	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    64	-/
    65	def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    66	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    67	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    68	  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0
    69	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>
    70	      fun x =>
    71	        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x
    72	        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x
    73	
    74	/-- The support invariant for a representation of a conditionally linear
    75	function.  This is a Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    76	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    77	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    78	-/
    79	def CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    80	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    81	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
    82	  | _, .zero, _ => True
    83	  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
    84	      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)
    85	
    86	/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
    87	encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    88	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    89	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    90	-/
    91	def IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    92	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
    93	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    94	  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,
    95	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S ∧ CondLinearTerm.eval t = L
    96	
    97	/--
    98	`IsCondLinear` abbreviates the full-coordinate predicate.  Blueprint
    99	`def:cl-func`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`; paper
   100	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
   101	-/
   102	def IsCondLinear (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
   103	  IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L
   104	
   105	/-- The zero conditionally linear function at every level, used to extend the
   106	family `R u` from the image `L(U)` to all indices in the concatenation

   108	private def CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   109	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] : (ell : ℕ) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
   110	  | 0 => .zero
   111	  | ell + 1 => .succ ∅ 0 (by simp) (fun _ => zeroOfLevel ell)
   112	
   113	@[simp]
   114	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_zeroOfLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   115	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ell : ℕ) (x : ι → K) :
   116	    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel (K := K) (ι := ι) ell) x = 0 := by
   117	  induction ell with
   118	  | zero => rfl
   119	  | succ ell ih =>
   120	      simp [CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel, CondLinearTerm.eval, ih]
   121	
   122	private theorem CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel_supportedOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   123	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ell : ℕ) (S : Finset ι) :
   124	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn
   125	      (CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel (K := K) (ι := ι) ell) S := by

401:+private def CondLinearTerm.concat {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
403:+    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]

409:+    {k : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιU) k →

421:+          intro x i hi
423:+          cases i with
425:+          | inl i =>
427:+              apply hSupport
429:+              simpa using hi

440:+    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]

454:+          (rTerm (acc + CondLinearTerm.eval t (fun i => x (.inl i))))

460:+  | zero =>

468:+      cases i <;>
470:+        simp [CondLinearTerm.concat, CondLinearTerm.eval, condLinearLiftLeft,

521:+        ext i

648:+/-- In a register partition, restricting a sum of supported vectors selects

660:+    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
662:+    (f : J → ι → K) (hf : ∀ j a, a ∉ V j → f j a = 0) (j : J) :

666:+  ext a
668:+  by_cases ha : a ∈ V j

678:+      apply hf i a
680:+      intro hai

684:+    · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim
686:+  · rw [coordinateRestriction]

    26		subset of the standard basis of $V$. Such a subspace is represented by an
    27		indicator vector $u \in \{0,1\}^s$, where $s = \dim(V)$, via

+/-- A representation of a conditionally linear function supported on a register
+takes values that vanish off that register.  This is a formalization-only
+auxiliary for `lem:cl-dist-prod`, blueprint `lem:cl-supported-vanishing`. -/
+theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_eq_zero_of_not_mem {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
+    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
+    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) (x : ι → K) {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ S) :
+    CondLinearTerm.eval t x a = 0 := by
+  induction t generalizing S with
+  | zero => rfl
+  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
+      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
+      change (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) +
+        CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x))) x) a = 0
+      rw [Pi.add_apply, hSupport _ a (fun haS₁ => ha (hS₁ haS₁))]
+      rw [ih _ (hrest _) (fun haDiff => ha (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp haDiff).1)]
+      exact zero_add 0
+
+/-- A supported representation of a conditionally linear function depends only
+on the coordinates in its register. -/
+private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_congr_of_eq_on {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
+    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
+    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) {x y : ι → K}
+    (hxy : ∀ a ∈ S, x a = y a) :
+    CondLinearTerm.eval t x = CondLinearTerm.eval t y := by
+  induction t generalizing S with
+  | zero => rfl
+  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
+      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
+      have hrestrict : coordinateRestriction S₁ x = coordinateRestriction S₁ y := by
+        ext a
+        by_cases ha : a ∈ S₁
+        · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha, hxy a (hS₁ ha)]
+        · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]
+      simp only [CondLinearTerm.eval, hrestrict]
+      rw [ih _ (hrest _) (fun a ha => hxy a (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp ha).1)]

+theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_coordinateRestriction {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
+    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
+    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) (x : ι → K) :
+    CondLinearTerm.eval t (coordinateRestriction S x) = CondLinearTerm.eval t x := by
+  exact CondLinearTerm.eval_congr_of_eq_on ht fun a ha => by
+    simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]

+    [DecidableEq ι] {S T : Finset ι} (hST : S ⊆ T) (x : ι → K) :

+  ext a
+  by_cases ha : a ∈ S

+  · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]

+    coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, f i) = f j := by

+  by_cases ha : a ∈ V j

+      intro hai

+    · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim
+  · rw [coordinateRestriction]
+    simp [ha, hf j a ha]
